title: The eighth king and Yosef's dreams: noga, the chashmal, and garments of light
overview: In the Torah of Rabbi Meir it was written *kosnos or*, garments of light with an *aleph*, and the chapter explains how the garments of skin become garments of light. Their root is the new *MaH*, the eighth king: the *bina* of *Tohu*. Rabbi Markel sees us living in his age, the age of science and of the internet, where every *sevara* is open to all. That openness is what connects the eighth king to Yosef who interprets dreams: in the dream of exile, Yosef puts the scattered letters back in order, an interjection from above, and people say, that's right. The garment of skin is the *chashmal*, the idea in letters, which can cover its meaning or reveal it. Its *kelipa* is *noga*: a light that looks bright only because of the darkness, like a candle at night or a diamond's sparkle, and also a sticking out, as the depth of an idea shows in a coarse *mashal* and G-dliness in a person who refines his body. A *chashmal* that lives on without the thought that made it is how *Tohu* continues, down to the *masach*. Repaired, the felt *yesh* becomes *ayin*, higher than *ayin* itself: the upper light.

terms.gloss: the eighth king of Tohu: the bina and tevuna of Tohu, which includes all seven kings and is past them; now, science
garments of light, with an aleph: the garments of skin (with an ayin) once the letters are put back in order and the mashal reveals the nimshal
Yosef who interprets dreams: Moshiach ben Yosef, who shows how it all fits together, an interjection from above in the eighth king's time
sortings; of the 288 sparks that fell with the scattered letters: putting the letters back together
the letters that come out of the outside of bina: an idea in letters that can be felt and passed on, and then lives on without the thought that made it
a mild glow, and a sticking out; the kelipa that comes from the chashmal, a light seen because of the darkness
sticking out: the second meaning of noga, light standing out in something physical but refined
a thought that sticks out so that it is felt, boiled out in the heart
somethingness, felt and sticking out: the noga of the ten sefiros, as in a conceited man or a felt fervor
the upper light: a light seen through a bright, shining garment, in which the souls see the radiance of the Shechina
confusion; of the letters, which is Tohu and the cause of the kelipos

sections.title: The eighth king of Tohu: science, the god of the age
sections.summary: The root of the repair is the new *MaH* of *Adam Kadmon*, called the eighth king. That king is the *bina* and *tevuna* of *Tohu*, and we live in his time: the age of science, whose method is *bina sheb'bina*, and of the internet, where every *sevara* is open to all.

phrases.he: (מו) אך הנה בתורתו של רבי מאיר היה כתוב כתנות אור באלף כו' כנזכר לעיל
להיות ידוע בשרש בחינת התיקון מבחינת שם מ"ה החדש דאדם קדמון כו', וכמו שכתוב במקום אחר שזהו בחינת מלך השמיני, שרש התיקון דמ"ה דחכמה כו'

blocks.text: The chapter goes back to what was said before: in the Torah of Rabbi Meir it was written *kosnos or* (garments of light) with an *aleph*. Its root is the new Name *MaH* of *Adam Kadmon*, which elsewhere is called the *melech hashmini* (the eighth king). Whatever explanations one reads on it, the eighth king is basically the *bina* and *tevuna* of *Tohu*. Look around the world and you see that we are in his time: the basic thing right now is the age of science.

Right now their god is science. Not even money: the ultimate god is science, already among Jews, even among *frum* Jews. If a thing cannot be made to agree with science, it doesn't hold. And the funny thing is that people say "science" and are not even really following science.

sensitivity.reason: Says that even frum Jews have made science their god.
sensitivity.publishable: Right now their god is science. Not even money: the ultimate god is science. If a thing cannot be made to agree with science, it doesn't hold. And the funny thing is that people say "science" and are not even really following science.

blocks.title: The earth and the sun go around each other
blocks.text: Even their science is a messed-up science. By their own theory, two bodies really go around each other; it is not that one stands still and the other moves. It is easy to see in a lab, or at a wedding: two men hold hands and spin, and both spin around the middle, where their hands are. When one is heavier, the center moves closer to it. Someone told him, he doesn't remember who, that the center of gravity of the earth and the sun is a little under the surface of the sun. The same with the earth and the moon: you can't really say the moon goes around the earth, and the tides prove it, since the moon pulls too.

blocks.title: Orbits like a screw
blocks.text: Most people think the sun stands still. A listener says it is an approximation; yes, but most people don't realize it. The sun moves toward the earth as the earth goes in its path: a double path. The planets pull the sun and each other, so the models with the sun in the middle and the planets on exact paths cannot be right: when Mars is on our side, the two pull each other a little out of their paths. And if the moon goes around the earth it moves the earth, so the earth does not go in a straight line but like a screw. A listener once saw, in a library, a book drawing the orbits by the old astronomy, the way people made fun of: like a pigtail, a screw, the beautiful designs of those spinning toys.

blocks.title: The sun in the center is only simpler
blocks.text: The only advantage of putting the sun in the center is that the orbits become more elegant, simpler to calculate. Even by their own theories of relativity it is *lav davka* (not necessarily so): it depends where you stand. Stand on earth and you can do the whole thing as if it all goes around the earth.

blocks.title: Galaxies, a black hole, and stars no telescope sees
blocks.text: It is a simplistic system. What about the galaxy Andromeda, or the stars? Everything pulls, and there is a center to the galaxy, which is really in Jerusalem, but that is beside the point. A listener brings the day's news: the center of the galaxy is a big black hole, seen swallowing about half of a star the size of our sun. That is one galaxy, among clusters of jillions of galaxies, and they don't know what is outside. The Mitteler Rebbe says there are infinite stars, and some *tzaddikim* could see stars beyond any telescope. Some huge mass out there could move the whole center of gravity. You don't really know.

What is really true is not what we are talking about. The point is that the god right now is the eighth king, science: the big god, the Nimrod. And the second god, money, depends on the first: Bill Gates and all that comes from science. Even the big money in music and opera depends on technology. In the days of Shakespeare, a girl singer could at most be a little traveling singer with pennies in her hat; such people become so big today because of technology. Without science you couldn't have the Beatles, not to mention electric music and the heavy metal beat.

What science really is, as was said before, is the scientific method. A real scientist knows it is not a philosophy or a body of knowledge but a methodology, and that methodology is *hisbonenus*: analysis, taking a thing apart into the components that make it up. Matter into atoms and the atomic table; the mind into its basic components in psychology; the same in physiology and biology. Then you come up with a *sevara*, an explanation: "It must be like this." They call it a theory, a hypothesis. Then, exactly as in the Talmud, you test it: in the case of coins found scattered, one says the owner gave up hope knowingly, another unknowingly, two *sevaros*, and the axiom they are tested against is the Mishna.

blocks.title: Blowing up the balloon
blocks.text: Science tests the *sevara* against physical reality. By your *sevara*, if we keep blowing up a balloon it should explode. Let's try it: boom, it explodes. That shows your *sevara* could be right, not that it is right; we only did not disprove it. If your *sevara* said the balloon would not explode, the explosion disproves it completely.
blocks.outOfPlace: The next side goes on with the eighth king of Tohu, the subject of line 2, before reading line 3.

blocks.text: That is *hisbonenus*, *bina sheb'bina*. And the scientific method we have today is not just the Greek way but the American way: *bina sheb'bina* with *tevuna sheb'tevuna*. The theories with a high probability of being right (to a scientist that only means several experiments did not disprove them) are applied to all kinds of things, to come up with the second god, sometimes really the first: *mamon* (money). The *bina sheb'bina* is applied for better solutions all the way down to earth, so that even the sheep can use theories they might not understand: drive a car, or get on a computer and talk to somebody on the other side of the world.
blocks.outOfPlace: The next side goes on with the eighth king of Tohu, the subject of line 2, before reading line 3.

sensitivity.reason: Calls people who use technology without understanding it "the sheep".

The *bina sheb'bina* is applied for better solutions all the way down to earth, so that even people can use theories they might not understand: drive a car, or get on a computer and talk to somebody on the other side of the world.

blocks.text: The text calls him the root of the repair of *MaH* of *chachma*, but that is the eighth king once he is fixed up, and the Kabbalistic books mostly take him as already fixed up, Yosef the master of dreams. Really he is a king of *Tohu*, though the root of the whole *Tikkun*. As the eighth he includes all seven and is way past them, *shelo b'erech* (beyond comparison), and things beyond comparison are coming from him today. We are very obviously in his kingdom, as he is in essence.
blocks.outOfPlace: The next side goes on with the eighth king of Tohu, the subject of line 2, before reading line 3.

blocks.text: He includes all the bad kings' things, so in a way it is much worse: the lust for money, the lewdness, conquering other nations, false *din*. All the emotional bad kings are now worse than ever, because the eighth includes them all. The lewdness was never at this point, and neither was its availability, and the availability of everything. There always was terrorism, but now the eighth king makes it available for one man to come up with what was done to the Twin Towers; in the old days they could not have done it.
blocks.outOfPlace: The next side goes on with the eighth king of Tohu, the subject of line 2, before reading line 3.

sensitivity.reason: A sweeping judgment of the present-day world, its lewdness worse than ever before.
sensitivity.publishable: He includes all the bad kings' things, so in a way it is much worse: the lust for money, conquering other nations, false *din*. All the emotional bad kings are now worse than ever, because the eighth includes them all, and everything is available. There always was terrorism, but now the eighth king makes it available for one man to come up with what was done to the Twin Towers; in the old days they could not have done it.

blocks.text: Yet the same eighth king is also the root of the repair, the *MaH* of *chachma*. Why? Because *hisbonenus*, as was learned in chapter one, will definitely get you to the truth slowly. It may first get you to the wrong *sevaros*, but you test them and don't just accept them. And what the eighth king makes available is available not just to Osama but to us. What we are doing would have been impossible even twenty years ago: we could not have reached so many people. Right now we are available to the world, literally, because of the eighth king of *Tohu*.
blocks.outOfPlace: The next side goes on with the eighth king of Tohu, the subject of line 2, before reading line 3.

blocks.title: The Nile of the eighth king: the internet
blocks.text: The eighth king is a total *Tohu* of ideas, and his Nile, his lifeblood, is the internet, what they call the information flow. He includes all the bad stuff, like the Tower of Babel: a tumult of many tongues and many ideas, a whole *bilbul* (confusion). Where do you find that nowadays? The internet, where everybody says different things. *Kishuf* (sorcery), lewdness, whatever you want, it's on the internet. And *davka* that is what is now giving it a possibility.
blocks.outOfPlace: The next side goes on with the eighth king of Tohu, the subject of line 2, before reading line 3.

blocks.title: Little green people behind me
blocks.text: Before the eighth king you could not know what somebody else was saying. But he considers all the opinions, even the wrong ones, and that is the whole thing of *bina sheb'bina*: to be a *sevara*, it does not have to be true. "I have a *sevara* that there are little green people walking behind me." Is that a *sevara*? Yes, and it is easily disproved: have somebody look behind me. Unless I come up with a new *sevara*: they're invisible.
blocks.outOfPlace: The next side goes on with the eighth king of Tohu, the subject of line 2, before reading line 3.

blocks.text: On the internet he compares all the *sevaros*, and anybody is free to. Before, you had to go by the regular *sevaros*: think another and "we'll kill you." Now all are allowed, so even *Kabbala*, forbidden when other things were allowed, is becoming allowed. That is why this same eighth king, the worst of the kings of *Tohu*, is also *Yosef poser chalomos*, Yosef who interprets dreams.
blocks.outOfPlace: The next side goes on with the eighth king of Tohu, the subject of line 2, before reading line 3.

sections.title: Yosef who interprets dreams: the exile is a dream
sections.summary: The eighth king, open to every *sevara*, is connected to Yosef who interprets dreams. The exile is a dream, now a nightmare; Yosef puts its letters into good combinations according to the original plan, an interjection from above that comes *davka* in the eighth king's time.

phrases.he: (והוא בחינת יוסף פותר חלומות

blocks.text: Does the eighth king actually change into Yosef? Given fifteen billion years, as they say, maybe. But he is connected to Yosef in that he gives an opening to everybody: there is no *sevara* he won't entertain. That is his saving grace: they are willing to listen to anybody, even to the rabbis.

Because of this, the craziest people are now starting to be attracted to rabbinical *Kabbala*. He also lets happen what the Rebbe said: before, you couldn't tell about the seven *mitzvos*; now you can, because it is the eighth king of *Tohu*. You can tell anybody anything. It is total, absolute *Tohu*, and *davka* he is Yosef who interprets dreams.

sensitivity.reason: Calls those newly drawn to Kabbala "the craziest people".
sensitivity.publishable: Because of this, all kinds of people are now starting to be attracted to rabbinical *Kabbala*. He also lets happen what the Rebbe said: before, you couldn't tell about the seven *mitzvos*; now you can, because it is the eighth king of *Tohu*. You can tell anybody anything. It is total, absolute *Tohu*, and *davka* he is Yosef who interprets dreams.

blocks.text: The eighth king is *bina*, and *bina* by its nature has to keep going through its conclusions and testing them. Sooner or later he finds something wrong with a conclusion, and tries another. This could take forever: there is no end to *meshugasn* (crazy notions). This theory is no good? Fine, here's another crazy theory. So it is a *chesed* that He is *Sha-dai*, who said *dai*, enough, to His world. What is the *dai*? The *Aibershter* wanted at first to create the world with *din* alone and had to inject *rachamim*: He put *tzaddikim* in every generation. That is the basic thing of *Moshiach ben Yosef*.
blocks.outOfPlace: From the addendum tape (tape 54), recorded after the chapter was finished, which goes back over its themes.

blocks.title: "Here, take a look at this"
blocks.text: *Moshiach ben Yosef* has to come *davka* in the time of the eighth king of *Tohu*, and he interjects the proper formula: "Here, look, this is what it is." It is an interjection, not an idea the eighth king came up with. The scientists will keep looking and finally figure it out, but it could take fifteen billion years or longer. He said enough. "Here, take a look at this," and people look and say, "Hey, that makes sense." That is Yosef who interprets dreams: there is a question, a scientific one, with various hypotheses, and he says, this is the one, this shows you the whole thing. Why there are waves and quanta, lights and vessels; why psychology works the way it does: these are the questions they are asking.
blocks.outOfPlace: From the addendum tape (tape 54), recorded after the chapter was finished, which goes back over its themes.

blocks.text: So the eighth king does not really turn into *Moshiach ben Yosef*, though the text talks as if he does. It has to come from a *tikkun* (repair) of the new *Shem MaH* of *Adam Kadmon*: a *tikkun* from upstairs. The *Aibershter* gave it over to us in His Torah, and the Rebbes brought it down. Right now we are making the *tikkun* of *Moshiach ben Yosef*, of Yosef who interprets dreams.
blocks.outOfPlace: From the addendum tape (tape 54), recorded after the chapter was finished, which goes back over its themes.

blocks.title: The baby in the basket on the Nile
blocks.text: Not that we figured it out with our great intellect. It was given to us by the Mitteler Rebbe, and really by the Rebbe, who gave us *Chassidus*, trained us first with *sichos* and *maamarim*, then gave us this book and the abilities to learn it. Then the *Aibershter* dumped us in the middle of the internet, the Nile of the eighth king, like the baby Moshe in a little basket on a big river: a teeny little thing floating in giant cyberspace. Who is even going to see us, to say we'll take over the world? Nonetheless, that is how it is working.
blocks.outOfPlace: From the addendum tape (tape 54), recorded after the chapter was finished, which goes back over its themes.

blocks.text: It is an injection of light from above, and it has to come *davka* in the time of the eighth king. He is not talking about abstract things: exile is a dream, and *Moshiach* will come and save us, an actual historical thing that is going to happen. One of the big *bilbulim* in understanding *Kabbala* and *Chassidus* is that people take it as something abstract that has nothing to do with "the price of tomatoes." This is the basic history of the world, and the eighth king and Yosef who interprets dreams are what is happening right now: we are in this dream of the exile.

blocks.text: Exile is likened to a dream, a kind of thought of the heart of *Zeir Anpin*, in sleep, when the *mochin* depart. Under the first seven kings people could fool themselves in the dream that it is reality, that it is normal to be like this. Now everybody knows something is wrong. The dream is no longer from the seven kings but from the eighth: not a nice little dream from this king or that one, but a total nightmare. Nobody knows what is going on or what happens next: absolute and total chaos.

phrases.he: ומאותיות שבדמיון החלום מצרף בהם צירופים טובים ומתוקנים
על פי מקור עומק החכמה דאדם קדמון שבמצחא כו'
phrases.en: *Davka* according to the *makor* of the *omek* of *chachma*, which is in the *pnimiyus* of *Adam Kadmon*

blocks.text: From the letters in the imagination of the dream he makes good, repaired combinations, **according to the *makor* of the *omek* of *chachma*, which is in the *pnimiyus* of *Adam Kadmon***: in the *mochin* of *Adam Kadmon*, which follow the *machshava kduma*, the original plan for the whole world. That is what Yosef does. Why is all this happening, why is it so crazy? He says: what do you mean? We are in the time of the eighth king of *Tohu*. What do you expect to happen?

blocks.text: *Tofer* and *poser* are one, as in "*Ben poras Yosef*." **And that's why he's called *Avrech***. One explanation: to bring down, from *birkayim* (knees), as in *yehei shmei rabba mevorach*, where *shmei rabba* is the *machshava kduma*, to be drawn down. Another: *av rach*, a father and a king; he is the father of the king.

sections.title: The letters put back together: from garments of skin to garments of light
sections.summary: Before the sorting, the big lights could not fit into a limited intellect and broke into crazy ideas; after the 288 sparks are sorted and the letters put back together, Yosef shows how it fits and the garments become light. The garment of skin is the *chashmal*, the idea embodied in letters, which can cover the *nimshal* or reveal it.

phrases.he: והיינו אחר הבירורים דרפ"ח ניצוצין שנפלו גם כן עם פירור ופיזור האותיות וכלים דתהו כנזכר לעיל,
phrases.en: Once you take these letters and put them back together again

phrases.he: בשכל המצומצם באות הנפרד,
ואז נקרא כתנות אור באלף.
phrases.en: And then the coverings become coverings of light

blocks.text: So is he Yosef, or the eighth king of *Tohu*? The eighth king is before the *birurim* (sortings). After the 288 sparks are sorted, once the scattered letters are put back together, he is Yosef. They scattered because the big lights could not fit into the *sechel hamtzumtzam* (the limited intellect), so it broke up into crazy ideas of *avoda zara*. People are trying to arrive at the truth, can't fit it into their brain, and come up with some crazy *meshugas*. Still, in his age they are trying to figure out what is going on.

That is the whole thing of *bina sheb'bina*: it wants to know the truth, and so does science. Pure science, not applied science, not *tevuna sheb'tevuna*, is wanting to know *davka* the truth. With the seven kings it is not like that: you don't care what the truth is, you just want the money, and you'll lie to get it. Here the whole thing is to get at the truth. But since it is a limited intellect in separate letters, it covers up the truth: it is *or* with an *ayin*. Then Yosef comes and tells them how it all fits together, and people say, oh, that's right! **And then the coverings become coverings of light**.

The eighth king is the worst king, yet he is the *bina* of *Tohu*, and in *bina* the *shevira* was not a full breaking. In the *Etz Chaim* and such works, hard as they are to understand, one thing is clear: in *Keser* of *Nekudim* there was hardly any breaking, in *chachma* a tiny bit, in *bina* a kind of breaking, but really the breaking is in the *uvchein* (the conclusion), not in the inner *bina*. The original analysis is correct.

blocks.text: There are a lot of people in the world, and the *uvchein* is that you should kill babies: that is what a *shevira* is. It is in the conclusion, not in the original analysis.

blocks.text: The same in the sciences: the observations and the analyses have no *shevira* in them. The *shevira* is in the conclusions they draw from them.

blocks.text: The garment of skin that clothes is called *chashmal*, and you can see the *chashmal* running around the world: all the demons running around with crazy ideas are *chashmals*. As was said, the *chashmal* comes from the outside of *bina*; it covers the *middos* and keeps the *midda* going. It is the idea without the brains, now in letters.

The terrorists run around wanting to do this and that; they are not sitting and thinking, "Wait a minute, is this business correct?" There is no *iyun* there. They accepted a *chashmal*, and the *chashmal* runs their life: a demon possessing them. The same with the missionaries trying to convert the Jews: if they would think about it... but they don't think about it; they go with the *chashmal*.

sensitivity.reason: Says the missionaries who try to convert Jews do not think and are run by a chashmal, like the terrorists.

blocks.text: It comes *davka* as *hagshama* (embodiment), as a *mashal* for a *nimshal*. The idea has to come into embodiment, and then people take the *mashal* for the *nimshal*, so the *mashal* covers the *nimshal* instead of revealing it. *Kesones or* with an *aleph* means that the *mashal* reveals the *nimshal*. The embodying of the intellect in much explanation, until a small child can grasp it, was all talked about earlier.

sections.title: Noga: a light that shines because it is dark
sections.summary: The *kelipa* of *noga* comes from the *chashmal*. Its light looks bright only because of the darkness, like a candle at night or the sparkle of a diamond, and the same holds for the depth of an idea, which shows most in a coarse, foreign *mashal*.

phrases.he: והוא בחינת נוגה,
phrases.en: And that's what *noga* is

phrases.he: כמו האור המאיר באפילה, שאורו ניכר שם יותר, עד שנראה אורו מבהיק ביותר מאור המאיר במקום אורה,
כמו שאמרו שרגא בטיהרא מאי מהני
phrases.en: A candle at noon time, what's it good for?

phrases.en: But in the middle of the night, when it's totally black, then a candle is very bright

phrases.he: והיינו לפי שהוא מאיר את החושך והאפילה דוקא

blocks.text: **And that's what *noga* is**: the *kelipa*, which comes from the *chashmal*. It is like a light shining in the dark, which shows more there, as they said: **a candle at noon time, what's it good for?** **But in the middle of the night, when it's totally black, then a candle is very bright**, and you can see everything with it, because it lights up *davka* the darkness.

That is like us. In older generations we would have been nothing, a candle at noon; in the days of Shlomo HaMelech nobody would have noticed us, we wouldn't even have reached the level of the Three Stooges. In our days we are like the only light around. It is so dark that the minute somebody sees our light they say, "Wow, look, there's a light," and it looks fantastically big.

phrases.he: שאי אפשר לומר באור הנר מצד עצמו שמבהיק אורו בעצם בחושך לילה יותר מביום,
phrases.en: You can't say: well, look at this candle, in the daytime it was hardly giving off light, and look how much light it's giving off now

phrases.he: רק מצד החושך שהוא היפוכו על כן ניכר בו יותר אור
phrases.en: It's just because of the *choshech* that is its opposite; therefore you can see the light more

phrases.he: ואין זו הבהקה אמיתית מצד עצמו,
phrases.en: It's not that it itself is really any brighter

phrases.he: רק שנראה לעין בהבהקה יותר, מפני החושך דוקא, שבו בא יתרון האור לעין הרואה לבד
phrases.en: There is a *yisron or* for the people who see it, *davka*

blocks.text: One cannot say of a candle: in the daytime it was hardly giving off light, and look how much light it gives off now. It gives off exactly the same light. It is only because of the darkness, its opposite, that you see more light in it. **It's not that it itself is really any brighter**; the advantage of the light is only for the eye of the one who sees it.

phrases.he: וזהו כמו הבהקת ובהירת אור האבן טוב, בהיותו מצוייר בגסות החומר, שהוא בהיר יותר משהוא מצוייר בחומר זך ובהיר כו' מטעם זה
phrases.en: That's why also the shining of a diamond is more shiny than shininess in the air

blocks.text: So too the shining of a precious stone set in coarse material. **That's why also the shining of a diamond is more shiny than shininess in the air**: the air is purer, but the sparkle shows *davka* in a diamond, because a diamond is a coarser thing.
When the sunlight shines through the air, the air is so refined that the light goes right through it. *Davka* a diamond sparkles, because it is *megusham* (physical).

phrases.he: (וכהבנת והשגת לתכלית עומק אור השכל במשל זר, שהוא ענין גס וזר דוקא מטעם זה כו')
phrases.en: You get the feeling and see the brightness of the *tachlis omek hasechel* *davka* in a very *gas mashal*, of a totally different thing

blocks.text: So too one grasps the utmost depth of the intellect in a foreign *mashal*, something coarse and foreign *davka*: **of a totally different thing**. The more you *megashem* (embody) the *mashal*, the more you see it. *Koach hatnua* (the power of movement) is already a foreign, embodied *mashal*, but when you embody it all the way and say "a cat," that is much more than saying *machshava kduma*, which is also really a *mashal*.

sections.title: The two meanings of noga: a glow, and a light that sticks out
sections.summary: *Noga* means a mild glow and it means sticking out, and both are one: light shows most where it meets something physical but refined, like the sun in a cloud, a gem in clear material, the light of the intellect in the letters of thought, or G-dliness in a person who refines his body.

phrases.he: וזהו בחינת נוגה שיש בו ב' פרושים כידוע
הא' מענין נוגה אור
phrases.en: A shining of light

phrases.he: או יגיה חשכי
phrases.en: He'll light up my darkness

phrases.he: וכהאי גוונא
והב' לשון בליטה לחוץ, וכמו שכתוב כאשר הוגה מן המסילה כו',
phrases.en: Somebody veers off the path

phrases.he: וכן ההוגה את יהו״ה כו'
phrases.en: Somebody who says the Name

phrases.he: וכמו הגיון שבמחשבה,
phrases.en: *Hegyon* means when the *machshava* sticks out in a way that you can feel it

phrases.he: כמו שכתוב והגית בו כו'
וכן והגיון לבי כו'
phrases.en: When the thought is boiled out in the heart

phrases.he: ושניהם עולין לכוונה אחת
phrases.en: The glow and the *blita* are really the same thing

blocks.text: *Noga* has two meanings. The first is **a shining of light**, as in "**He'll light up my darkness**": not a bright light but a mild shining, a glow. The second is *blita*, sticking out: as one veers off the path, or pronounces the Name, and *hegyon*, a thought that sticks out so that you feel it, boiled out in the heart. **The glow and the *blita* are really the same thing**: a glow too is light sticking out.

phrases.he: כמו שכתוב במקום אחר על דרך דוגמא מאור השמש המאיר בענן, שאורו מוכפל שם, וניכר הוא שם ביותר משניכר בגוף השמש עצמו
phrases.en: When the light shines through the cloud, then you can actually see the ray of light

phrases.he: כי מפני הזדככות גשם הענן שבהרכבת חלקי המים שבו, יוכר שם האור בכל פרטי חלקיו ביותר
phrases.en: When it turns into the rainbow, you can actually see the parts

phrases.he: כמו ג' גווני קשת שנקרא מראה הנוגה,
phrases.en: That's called the *mar'eh hanoga*

phrases.he: כמו שכתוב כמראה הקשת כו', כן מראה הנוגה כו'

blocks.text: Like the sun shining in a cloud, where its light is doubled and shows more than in the body of the sun itself. **When the light shines through the cloud, then you can actually see the ray of light**, and that it travels in a straight line. With no cloud it just looks like there is light everywhere, and in the body of the sun you can't see a light separate from the sun at all. More than that, **when it turns into the rainbow, you can actually see the parts**, which you can't see without it.

The three colors of the rainbow are called **the *mar'eh hanoga***. Because it is a *noga*, it has to go through a thing, and so, like the rainbow, it breaks the light up so that you can see its parts.

phrases.he: וכמו פרטי חלקי גוונין שבאבן טוב, לא ניכר יפה כל כך כי אם בהיותו מורכב באיזה חומר, אך לא בחומר גס, אלא בחומר זך וצלול שיבהיק אורו ביותר
וכך הוא ענין הב' בפירוש נוגה, שהוא בחינת הבליטה בגשם זך
phrases.en: The sticking out *davka* in a *geshem zach*

phrases.he: שנזדכך קצת,
phrases.en: That it's a little bit purified

phrases.he: שם בולט והוגה האור כמו יגיה חשכי דוקא

blocks.text: So too the colors in a precious stone show their beauty only when it is set in some material, not a coarse one but a pure, clear one. That is *kelipas noga*: not totally coarse like the *kelipos hatuma* (the impure husks), but *davka* a material, a pure one. A piece of lead won't sparkle. Air won't sparkle either; the light just goes right through it. It has to be a material, and a pure one.

That is the second meaning of *noga*: **the sticking out *davka* in a *geshem zach***, a pure physical thing, as the light sticks out in the diamond: a material **a little bit purified**, where it lights up the darkness.

phrases.he: וכן הגיון שבמחשבה עיונית, שבא אור השכל בבחינת בליטה לחוץ בגשם האותיות שבהרהור המחשבה, שאז דוקא ניכר ומושג הארת עומק השכל יותר
וזה שכתוב והגית בו כו'
phrases.en: To do the *hisbonenus* in a way of bringing it down into the *meshalim*

phrases.he: והיינו גם כן כמו ענין המשלים, שבולט ומושג שם אור השכל יותר כנזכר לעיל

blocks.text: So too *hegyon* in analytical thought: the light of the intellect sticks out in the physical letters of thought, and *davka* there the depth is felt. And so with people. If you need material, you have animals; if you need refinement, you have angels. Neither works. What you need is people, who have to purify themselves, and *davka* then the divine light shines the most: people in a physical, animal body, not angels, who refine the animal nature. *Davka* there is the big sticking out of *Elokus*.

In analytical thought too, it is *davka* when the *iyun* is drawn out at length, brought down into letters and *meshalim*, that the depth of the intellect sticks out more. That is "*vehagisa bo*": **to do the *hisbonenus* in a way of bringing it down into the *meshalim***, as with the *meshalim* above, where the light of the intellect sticks out and is grasped more.

phrases.he: והוא בחינת נוגה דעשר ספירות כו' בכלל,
שזהו בחינת הישות המורגש ובולט
phrases.en: The actual physical somethingness that is felt and sticks out

phrases.he: (על דרך המבואר במקום אחר בענין ראית איש חכם בעיניו כו',
phrases.en: A person who is wise in his own eyes: a conceited person

phrases.he: וכן ופלגשו ושמה ראומה, ראו שאני בטל כו',
phrases.en: Look what a *ma* I am, look at me, how holy I am

phrases.he: וכהתלהבות אלהי״ת המורגשת כו')
phrases.en: A felt *hislahavus* of *Elokus*

blocks.text: The *noga* of the ten *sefiros* is the *yeshus*, **the actual physical somethingness that is felt and sticks out**: one wise in his own eyes, a conceited *yesh*; *re'u ma* in the *Yalkut Shimoni*, look how *batel* I am, how holy; or **a felt *hislahavus* of *Elokus***, which the *Kuntres HaHispaalus* says to stay away from. It is *davka* when you refine that *yesh* that the divine light really sticks out.

sections.title: The chashmal: letters with a life of their own, down to the screen
sections.summary: The *chashmal* comes from the outside of *bina*: letters that stick out and can be passed on, until they live without the thought that made them. It shelters the *middos* like a mother's wings, and as it coarsens it becomes the *masach*, the partition between *Atzilus* and *Beriya*.

phrases.he: וכל זה שרש בחינת החשמל שנעשה מחיצוניות דבינה
phrases.en: This whole thing is the *shoresh* of the *chashmal*: the *chashmal* comes out from *chitzoniyus* of *bina*

blocks.text: **This whole thing is the *shoresh* of the *chashmal***, which comes from the outside of *bina*: the letters that stick out. Then the *chashmal* has its own life. It is passed on and becomes the next person's *ratzon* without his even thinking about it: a whole will made up with no *hisbonenus* in the first place. That is how *Tohu* continues.

So it tends to deteriorate, as Rashi and the commentators explain about the early generations. A first generation makes up *meshalim* to *chap* the light better; the *chashmal* is passed on, and by the third or fourth generation it is a broken-telephone effect: they grasp the outside of the *mashal* and don't know what it relates to. That is how the Rambam explains how *avoda zara* started in the first place, and it is not only *avoda zara*.

Even really bad stuff like communism, in a way, started off from a good intention. So do a lot of these things, like abortion: it starts with a good intention and ends up as killing your own children, the worst possible thing that could happen.

sensitivity.reason: Political opinions: communism, and abortion called killing your own children.

blocks.title: Eating the children
blocks.text: He recalls, with a listener, the story from the time of the Tree of Knowledge that the Satan gave them a child and they ate him. That is basically it now. People don't want to have the kids, because the *parnassa* (livelihood) will get less: they are eating the kids. The same with the way national credit works: building up debt that goes to the next generation is eating your kids, in a way.

sensitivity.reason: Says people who have fewer children for the sake of income, and a nation that runs up debt, are eating their children.
sensitivity.publishable: He recalls, with a listener, the story from the time of the Tree of Knowledge that the Satan gave them a child and they ate him. A good intention can end up like that: eating your own children.

blocks.text: The whole chapter is about how this comes about, through the separation of the letters and the *chashmal*. The *chashmals* in people's minds are ideas made of letters that travel from father to son, until the idea has a life of its own, separate from the intellect that made it. How? As he explains, the source of the *chashmal* is higher than the intellect itself.
blocks.outOfPlace: From the addendum tape (tape 54), recorded after the chapter was finished, which goes back over its themes.

blocks.text: This ties in with what the *Shaarei Ora* says about *teshuva*: do it in the *middos* and it won't help, you have to do it in the *sechel*; that won't help either, you have to do it in the *ratzon* and the *taanug*. Even then the letters can come back. They are still there, with a life of their own, and cannot even be destroyed. What he finally tells you is to wash them with tears: you can't get rid of them; you can only cleanse them and put them into proper order.
blocks.outOfPlace: From the addendum tape (tape 54), recorded after the chapter was finished, which goes back over its themes.

blocks.title: Letters of cow manure and a Swiss bank account
blocks.text: The proper order has its own advantage even when the letters are not cleansed. *Chassidus* explains that besides their order, the letters themselves can be dirty: the letters of a lustful thought are in the wrong order and are *mamash* dirty. But say I give you, written in letters made of cow manure, the number of a Swiss bank account with ten billion dollars in it. Does that detract from the account? Not at all. That is why the letters of *Chassidus* can take even letters of cow manure and tell you about a bank account with ten billion dollars: the order of the letters can supersede the impurity of the letters themselves.
blocks.outOfPlace: From the addendum tape (tape 54), recorded after the chapter was finished, which goes back over its themes.

sensitivity.reason: A coarse image: letters made of cow manure.
sensitivity.publishable: The proper order has its own advantage even when the letters are not cleansed. *Chassidus* explains that besides their order, the letters themselves can be dirty: the letters of a lustful thought are in the wrong order and are *mamash* dirty. But say I give you, written in letters made of mud, the number of a Swiss bank account with ten billion dollars in it. Does that detract from the account? Not at all. That is why the letters of *Chassidus* can take even letters of mud and tell you about a bank account with ten billion dollars: the order of the letters can supersede the impurity of the letters themselves.
sensitivity.publishableTitle: Letters of mud and a Swiss bank account

phrases.he: (שמזה נעשו בחינת הכנפיים,
כמו שכתוב על גוזליו ירחף כו',
אימא פרישת גדפהא כו',
phrases.en: The mother spreads her wings over the chickies

phrases.he: ונקרא כנפי שכינה שמשם שרש נשמות הגרים כו'
phrases.en: That's where the *neshamos* of the *geirim* come from

phrases.he: וזהו גם כן ענין מאמר הזהר על פסוק בקר אערך לך ואצפה, דוד אתקין האי חופאה לחפאה בקר דיוסף כו'
phrases.en: David made this *chupa* to cover up the *boker* of Yosef, of *yesod*

phrases.he: ועביד נהורא לאתלבשא כו'
phrases.en: And makes a light to become clothed in

phrases.he: עד אינון דאקרון כנפין עילאין כו' כמו שכתוב ביאורו במקום אחר)

blocks.text: From this come the wings, the wings of *bina*: "over its young it hovers," *Imma* spreads her wings. **The mother spreads her wings over the chickies**, over the *middos*: as was said, the *chashmal* of *bina* is what protects the *midda*.

blocks.title: The Hatfields and the McCoys
blocks.text: A basic *mashal* for the *chashmal* of *bina* is the Hatfields and the McCoys. The *chashmal* holds the hatred in place, though they no longer even know what the original incident was. It is just the *uvchein* from the outside of *bina* that keeps the *midda* in place.
These are called the wings of the *Shechina*: **that's where the *neshamos* of the *geirim* come from**, the souls of converts.

The *Zohar* on "In the morning I will set out for You": **David made this *chupa* to cover up the *boker* of Yosef, of *yesod***. That is, *Malchus* covers the light of *yesod*, **and makes a light to become clothed in**, up to those called the upper wings. He does not know this passage of the *Zohar*; it is brought here as speaking of the same matter.

phrases.he: עד שמזה נשתלשל ויורד עוד להיות בבחינת המסך ממש,
הנקרא פרסא המפסיק ומבדיל בין אצילות לבריאה כו',
והמלכות בוקע המסך (כמו שיתבאר)
phrases.en: And then the *Malchus* can go through the *masach*

blocks.text: From this it comes down further, to an actual *masach* (screen). The *chashmal* of *bina* starts as a *kosnos or* with an *aleph*, refining and clarifying the thought, and turns into one with an *ayin*: the *grobkeit* (coarseness) grows until the pure material is murky, a *masach* over the light. This is how *Tohu* came to be, as with the king of *Tohu* at the chapter's start: it covered more and more, until the *middos* were of *Tohu* and finally even the *bina*.
blocks.outOfPlace: He reads the first half of line 33 here (w2202), after the Zohar of line 32; the alignment mark falls on its second half.

blocks.text: And now it is even worse than in past generations, so the *middos* are worse too. Things that were lewd even back then, like *maaseh Mitzrayim* (the practices of Egypt), are not considered *maaseh Mitzrayim* anymore; they are considered actually goodness. A person who is against it is told: what do you mean, you hate people? If you're against it, you're bad, a bigot. He is describing here how the generation got there.

sensitivity.reason: An oblique jab at present-day sexual morality (maaseh Mitzrayim) and at those who call its opponents bigots.
sensitivity.publishable: And now it is even worse than in past generations, so the *middos* are worse too: what was considered lewd even back then is now considered goodness. He is describing here how the generation got there.

blocks.text: The eighth king will turn into Yosef and straighten it out by putting the letters of *chashmal* back in place, since they came out of the upper thought to clarify the light. Then they got mixed up, division after division, until it was an actual *masach*, the *parsa* between *Atzilus* and *Beriya*. **And then the *Malchus* can go through the *masach***.

sections.title: Garments of light with an aleph: the yesh that becomes ayin
sections.summary: When the *noga* of the *chashmal* is repaired through the new *MaH*, the felt *yesh* turns into *ayin*, and a *yesh* that is *ayin* is higher than *ayin* itself. That is the *zihara ila'a*, a light seen through a bright garment, which this explained, coarse learning is to become.

phrases.he: אך ענין כתנות אור באלף, הוא אחר התיקון ובירור דבחינת נוגה דחשמל
שהוא על ידי בחינת ביטול העצמי דמ"ה החדש דאדם קדמון כו',
phrases.en: Through the new *Shem MaH* of *Adam Kadmon*

phrases.he: שרש התיקון הנזכר לעיל,
עד שנהפך בחינת היש המורגש דנוגה בבחינת ביטול לאין ממש כו'
phrases.en: Until the felt *yesh* of *noga*, in a way of *bittul*, turns to actual *ayin*

phrases.he: וכאשר היש הוא בבחינת אין, הרי הוא יותר נעלה מבחינת אין דמ"ה שבחכמה המברר כו'
phrases.en: Then it's even higher than when the *ayin* is an *ayin*

phrases.he: כמו שכתוב במקום אחר

blocks.text: *Kesones or* with an *aleph* comes after the repair and sorting of the *noga* of the *chashmal*: through the eight kings of *Tohu* turning over, **through the new *Shem MaH* of *Adam Kadmon***. That is a new name for the *middos*, since *MaH* is basically the name of the *middos*. It is also *koach MaH*: the *middos* are *batel* to the intellect. Like a *baal teshuva* (penitent), who comes up with a new idea of what his *middos* should be.

**Until the felt *yesh* of *noga*, in a way of *bittul*, turns to actual *ayin***. Not just that *ayin*: a *yesh* that is an *ayin*. **Then it's even higher than when the *ayin* is an *ayin***. That is also how *bina* can go higher than *chachma*: when *bina* gets to the *ayin*, it gets there as a *yesh*, so that you can *mamash* explain the whole thing.

phrases.he: על כן נקרא כתנות אור כמו עוטה אור כשלמה כו'
שהוא בחינת אור דתורה לאחר הבירור דמ"ה דחכמה עילאה, שמברר לבחינת ב"ן דנוגה,
phrases.en: The light of the Torah makes the *birurim* of *chachma ila'a* that is *mevarer* the *BaN* of *noga*

phrases.he: שעולה למעלה מבחינת מ"ה כו'
phrases.en: It brings the *Shem BaN* up to *SaG*

phrases.he: (כידוע דס"ג שהוא גס ,בו היה השבירה,
phrases.en: *SaG*, when it's broken, is called *gas*, and the *shevira* was *davka* in the *bina*, in the *chitzoniyus* of *bina*

phrases.he: הרי לאחר הבירור דב"ן שנפל משבירת הכלים, עולה בשרשו בבחינת ס"ג כו' שלמעלה משם מ"ה כו')

blocks.text: So they are called garments of light. **The light of the Torah makes the *birurim* of *chachma ila'a* that is *mevarer* the *BaN* of *noga***, sorting out *Asiya* all the way, till it is a fixed-up Torah thing. **It brings the *Shem BaN* up to *SaG***, above *MaH*. *SaG*, broken, is called *gas* (coarse): the breaking was in the outside of *bina*.

phrases.he: ונקרא זיהרא עילאה,
phrases.en: And then it's called the upper light

phrases.he: על דרך משל אור המזוכך ביותר בלבוש זך ובהיר עד מאד, שעל ידו דוקא יכולים להסתכל בתוספת הבהירות והבהקה בעין
היפך הענין דנגה קודם הבירור, שהוא בהסתר החשך, רק שמצד יתרון האור בחשך הוא נראה אור מבהיק כו'
phrases.en: Why do you see any light there at all? Because it's so dark

blocks.text: Then it is called *zihara ila'a*, **the upper light**: like a very refined light in a pure, bright garment, through which *davka* one can look at its added brightness. It is the opposite of *noga* before the sorting, which is in the hiddenness of darkness: **why do you see any light there at all? Because it's so dark**. But afterwards the *chashmal* of *noga* will go up and be higher than the light itself, higher than the light of *chachma*.

That is what is happening here. Right now we have a tiny bit of light, seen only because of the darkness. But it is going to happen: the light we are making by bringing these matters *davka* into total coarseness, like cats, will rise to a supernal light bigger than the light of the revealed Torah, a light of a *yesh*. Everybody has the idea that it can't be explained, only experienced, and that only a great *tzaddik* could see it. Yes, in the olden days, when it was as an *ayin*. We are going to have it as a *yesh*, deeper than the original *ayin*, and still an *ayin*. How? Look at this whole thing: total *yeshus*, an explanation, and yet the actual G-dly *ayin*, going even higher, into the true *yesh*, the essence of the source of light.

blocks.text: Here the shining is from the essence of the light: not a tiny light that looks shiny in the dark, but a lot of light, the garment itself made of bright light, called *ispaklaria d'nehara*. *Ispaklaria* is spectacles, a lens: like the doctor's instrument for looking in your ear, with a light in it to see in a dark place. **This is called the upper light**, through which the souls see the radiance of the *Shechina* in *Gan Eden*, and really even higher.

Chapter 46 has several very important matters, and they are all related, which is why they are together. It all goes around the *chashmal* and the letters. *Tohu* is here, the eighth king of *Tohu* and how he turns into *Moshiach ben Yosef*, the exile and the dreams, the sleep of *Zeir Anpin*; and he explains *noga* and the beginning of the *kelipos*. The basic matter of *Tohu* and the *kelipos* is that the letters are mixed up.

blocks.question: A student called from Israel: the text says there are three levels in speech, but he saw only two, the material and the letters.
blocks.text: In letters there are two levels: the letters themselves, an *aleph*, a *beis*, a *gimmel*, and the letters in order, the *tzura* (form) of the speech. So in actual speech there are three things you hear: the *chomer* (material), the raw sound of the voice; the letters, the components made of that material; and the order they are put into, the final form of the words, which is what you understand. If he were really drunk, slurring his letters and mixing them up, you might not understand what he is saying.

It is the same in thought: the components, which are the letters, and the final form. And the components are not just an *aleph* or a *beis*: they are put into bigger components, letters, words, sentences. Mix the words of a sentence around, or put a comma in a different place, and you can change the meaning from one thing to the total opposite.

The form comes from *Malchus* of *tevuna*: it is really in the intellect. But speech, or thought once it is a separate thing, talking inside your head, is a *chashmal*, not the original. It comes out of *bina* as actual letters that can be felt and passed on; that is its good part. But in letters of *chashmal* the *bilbul* can come in.

There are kinds of *bilbul*. One is where the letters actually get mixed up. Another, not so bad, but it can turn out just as bad or worse: an idea comes out of *Malchus* of *tevuna* as an application for a certain framework of time or space, and the *chashmal* goes on existing past the time it applies to. Like people in a reactionary idea, acting by reflex, not seeing how it applies to what is coming out now. That is the *bilbul* and the kingdom of *Tohu*.

*Tohu* was the *bilbul* of the letters, and this *bilbul* causes the *kelipos*: they come out of the *chashmal*, as he explains here what *noga* is. From the *noga* comes an even bigger *bilbul*, until the *noga* is just a *masach*.

blocks.title: A book you don't understand and the Communist Manifesto
blocks.text: The difference between the *masach* of *noga* and the *masach* of the *kelipos hatuma*: the *masach* of *noga* is like this book. It is in proper order, yet a lot of people look at it and don't understand it; it covers the idea, but itself it is in order, and if you read it you get the right order. Then there is a thing whose order is messed up, so that even if you understand it, it means the wrong thing altogether, like the Communist Manifesto. With *noga*, nothing is wrong with it, it could be *kedusha* (holiness), but you don't understand it. The other is total *tuma* (impurity) even if you do understand it.

Before learning it as *bina*, he wanted to put it, as at the beginning of the book in chapters one and two, in the way of *tevuna*: applied down to here. He is not talking about *chashmals* as something up there, the holy *chashmal*. You can see the *chashmals* floating in people's brains. The rest of the chapter we all know: the candle at noon, the precious stone, that it is *davka* when you bring it into physicality that it glows.

blocks.text: But the final thing of the *kosnos or* is not a candle that doesn't glow so much and is seen only because it is dark. It is going to turn into a big light, a real big light. That is the whole business of what is going to happen: the *kosnos or* with an *ayin* turning into one with an *aleph*.

reviewQuestions.question: Why is the eighth king of *Tohu* both the worst of the kings and the root of the repair?
How is Yosef who interprets dreams connected to the eighth king, and does the eighth king really turn into him?
Why does a candle look brighter at night, and what does that teach about *noga*?
What are the two meanings of *noga*, and why are they really one?
How does a *chashmal* come to have a life of its own, and how does that keep *Tohu* going?
Why is a *yesh* that becomes *ayin* higher than *ayin* itself?
